chunks: Humeed ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abu Al-Maghra' from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

When the boy reaches ten years, if he bequeaths a third of his wealth rightfully, his bequest is valid. And if he is a boy of seven years, and he bequeaths a small amount from his wealth rightfully, his bequest is valid.
ai.seo_question: What is the age of legal capacity for a minor to make a will in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the legal capacity of minors for testamentary bequests, distinguishing between a ten-year-old who may bequeath one-third of their wealth and a seven-year-old permitted only a smaller portion. It reflects the Shia juristic view that pre-pubescent children possess limited legal agency, allowing them to dispose of a fraction of their assets provided the bequest is made to a rightful recipient.
